source_en: Returning to open the salon for morning appointments.
Picking up a shipment of imported hair product from the depot.
Visiting a client in the residential block for a home styling session.
Bartering salon services for food and medicine at the market.
Searching the district for any remaining beauty supply stock.
Returning from a supply run. The city has no conditioner left anywhere.
Keeping the salon open for whoever still comes. Someone always does.
Bringing the last medical-grade filler back to the salon.
Going home to finish a procedure I started this morning.
Clerk at the tram ticket office. Home after the morning shift.
First professional haircut of my life. Booked at a barber's.
Picking up my maternity leave papers.
Selling off the salon chairs. Looks never mattered to me.
Visiting my grandchildren in the eastern block.
Applying for work at the bread factory. My salon shut in May.
Throwing out every mirror I own. Appearances are vanity.
Collecting my pension. Forty years of cutting hair is enough.
Asked the polyclinic to undo everything. I want my old face.
Officer! Your eyebrows are doing something very interesting today. In a good way... mostly. Have you considered threading?
Ah, back again! I have been testing a new under-eye technique. Tell me honestly, can you see the bruising?
Here are my papers. While I have you: do you moisturise? This air is absolutely destroying everyone's pores.
I did a new procedure last night. Do not be alarmed by the swelling. It is part of the process.
You look tired, officer. I have something for that. Here, take a card. First session is free.
The salon is still open. We are the last beauty service running in this district. That means something.
Do not stare. I know it looks dramatic. Beauty requires sacrifice, and I am very committed.
I have been refining my jaw all week. The symmetry is almost perfect. Almost.
Something is wrong with the mirrors in this city. They have all started lying.
You are STARING at me. Do not. Stare. At. Me.
I can see exactly what you think of my face right now. It is written all over yours. You are wrong.
I look incredible. Say it. I need you to say it before I let you stamp anything.
This? This is an improvement. Each one is an improvement. Stop making that face at me.
I have been optimising. Non-stop. You could never understand what it takes.
You do not get to judge me. Nobody gets to judge me anymore. Stamp it and look away.
I am the most beautiful thing left in this city. Everything else has rotted. I am still here. I am STILL PERFECT.
My face is not finished. None of this is finished. Stop looking at it like it is finished.
I know what I look like. I KNOW. And it is FINE. Everything is fine. Stamp it.
Wonderful! Come by the salon sometime. You have good raw material. I could do a lot with it.
Smart choice, officer. Judgement is a two-way street. Remember that.
You passed me through. Good. You have good instincts. Or good taste, at least.
Excuse me?! Do you have any idea who does the hair for half this district?!
This is because of how I LOOK, isn't it. Admit it. ADMIT IT.
I am not going in there. My face is not done yet. I absolutely refuse.
But... I still had... so much left... to fix...
My face... no... it was almost... symmetrical...
I was... so close... to perfect...
This is aesthetic discrimination and I will be filing a formal complaint.
Fine. FINE. But when I come out I will look INCREDIBLE, and you will feel terrible about this.
I have tweezers in my pocket. You cannot stop the process.
I was… so close… to the jawline I wanted…
Nobody… ever appreciated… how much work went into this…
It just needed… one more… adjustment…
Where are you coming from?
The salon on Rustaveli. Two perms, a colour, and my own jaw between clients. Exhausting, but worth it.
The market by the river. I traded a haircut for filler from a man with Polish labels. Do not tell anyone.
The salon. I keep it open for whoever still comes. And I was working on myself. I lost track of the hours.
My salon on Plekhanov Avenue. Small place, but the light is good for colour work.
The barracks canteen. I cut hair for the soldiers now. The salon closed weeks ago, like all the others.
Home. I shut the salon for good last month. There is no one left worth cutting.
The supply depot. They still have what I need. Do not ask what. You would not understand the list.
From the mirror. I have been working on myself. Non-stop. It is a full-time commitment and I do not expect you to understand.
I do not remember leaving. I was in the mirror for a long time. Time moves differently when you are focused.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
Bruising along the jaw. Self-administered filler, last Thursday. It settles by Sunday. I have done this twelve times.
Some swelling. A little numbness in the cheeks. My pain threshold has gone up, which I take as a very good sign.
I cannot feel my cheekbones. I sleep badly. Neither matters. The proportions are finally correct.
Nothing. I have never had a procedure in my life, officer. This is all natural. Good genes.
No swelling at all. A surgeon at the polyclinic did my last injection. Very professional, very clean.
I feel wonderful. I stopped all procedures a month ago. I have not touched my face since.
I told you. No symptoms. These are improvements. There is a significant difference.
Everyone keeps calling them symptoms. They are not symptoms. They are upgrades.
My body is cooperating fully with the vision. That is all you need to know.
Your skin is dehydrated, officer. Drink water. Use SPF. I am genuinely begging you.
I opened the salon at six this morning. I will close it when the city does.
A man came in yesterday asking for the post-apocalyptic look. I gave him a trim and sent him home.
The good products are all gone from the shelves. I have been improvising. The results are mostly fine.
People keep telling me I look different. I look optimised. There is a difference.
Certain fillers can still be sourced from the medical quarter if you know the right people. I know the right people.
The mirror in my salon cracked this morning. I took it as a challenge.
Everyone in this city has stopped caring about how they look. It is deeply upsetting to witness.
I am not finished. I want to be clear about that. What you are seeing is a work in progress.
Stop looking at my face. I can see you looking.
I know what I look like. I am the only one who gets to decide what that means.
You have an opinion about my face. I can tell. Keep it to yourself.
I rate everyone I meet on sight. You are not performing as well as you think you are.
Perfect. Almost perfect. Getting closer every single day.
I am the last beautiful thing left in this district. Someone has to be.
